role: Replaces the flat crater SM_SpiritWound_01. TG-T0-ASSETS Q2 (Lead, 2026-10-02): a vertical wound, not a hole. Shares the shrine's read - tall thin vertical with a see-through gap - so the whole spirit family announces itself by one shape.

assembly_read.whole: the union of all modules: a tall thin vertical with an open gap you can see daylight through

design_notes.why_asymmetric: The right post is shorter and the lintel is broken, so it reads as DAMAGED rather than built. A symmetrical gate would read as a shrine - a thing that works - and this is a wound, which is a thing that was broken. Asymmetry is the entire difference between 'portal' and 'injury'.
design_notes.why_a_gap: The locked spirit signature is 'tall thin vertical WITH a see-through gap'. The gap is load-bearing and is not a proportion - it is the one family whose signature no amount of resizing can satisfy (TG-GRAYBOX-SILHOUETTE Q8).
design_notes.why_the_glow_is_inside: The glow sits IN the gap, not on a plate above it, so light reads as coming through the break. A flat glow plate was the crater's tell and is what made the old volume read as ground rather than as spirit.

replaces.why: A 3x3x0.35 crater with a 1.8x1.8x0.2 glow plate measured band 'flat'. Spirit requires 'tall'. The crater could not satisfy that without becoming a different object, which is the fork TG-T0-ASSETS Q2 was opened for.

measured_target.note: 0.18 posts on a 1.1 plinth, 2.4 tall. The plinth is wide relative to the posts, which is what previously pulled the assembly into 'mid' - the shrine fix narrows its base for the same reason. Verify with graybox_spec_reader.py, do not trust this number.

open_questions: Q2 answered the shape. It did not answer whether the wound is the SAME object as a shrine or a sibling: if a player reaches a shrine and a wound, are they meant to read as the same kind of thing? Both are now tall-thin-with-a-gap. Sharing a silhouette is what makes the family legible; it may also make the two places feel interchangeable. Queued for Round 2.
